R3 control rows; paired medians -50% actions / -40% tokens / -30% wall vs strongest comparable baseline; zero fabricated successes; two-pass replication), explicit kill conditions, internal-only scope (~30-60 rows), and 'a clean loss is an acceptable PB-001 outcome'. Hypothesis board seeded PH-1 PRODUCT_CANDIDATE / PH-2 WATCH (capability registry line) / PH-3 REJECTED (physics double-negative) / PH-4 WATCH.

BETA ARCHITECT froze PB-001 v1 (status READY, benchmark_frozen=true) honoring every cited Graph mechanism at its audited strength: one runtime three arms (B0 cold ReAct agent / B1 trajectory-memory AWM-class / B2=SPIDER) byte-equal by construction with a B0-validity gate (smoke-fail => MEASUREMENT_INVALID) and B1-primacy comparator rule; vendored file list pinned to lab/graph@d41fe9b with per-file adaptation limits and regression fixtures; KB/experience symmetry so SPIDER-vs-B1 is a clean test of packaging; frozen panel 10 tasks x 3 arms x 2 passes = 60 rows across R1/R2/R3 with independently authored goal texts, harness-judged anchored predicates + nav-chain integrity, byte-restored write-suppressed KB per row, perf_counter/token/call instrumentation under hard compute caps; win rule = director floor verbatim PLUS three strictness tightenings (explicit R3 degradation bound, reused-share >=50% on memory-solved rows, per-row suppression assertion); 10 component-level failure classes mapped to isolating flags for assumptions A1-A5; freeze checkpoints F1/F2 (post-F2 changes quarantine results as exploratory). Live-site probes confirmed both demo sites healthy at byte sizes identical to audited prefights.

ROOT CAUSE LOG-ONLY: BETA BUILDER session terminated by permission auto-rejection at 05:54:29Z. The agent ran an environment-probing compound command touching ~/.config, ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json etc.; opencode emitted 'permission requested: external_directory (/home/runner/.local/share/opencode/*); auto-rejecting' then 'Error: The user rejected permission to use this specific tool call.' and the session ended. The workflow validator then failed with '::error::Missing product_beta_build state' (exit 1), skipping tester/auditor/director jobs. This is the SECOND confirmed instance of the permission-abort-kills-whole-session mechanism (first: Graph run 32782331702, CF-2026-08-25-05) and the first inside product-loop.yml. Before aborting, the builder had done useful work worth preserving as context: verified architect snapshot == repo; discovered working-tree graph/+shared/ files are STRIPPED-DOWN variants vs pinned d41fe9b (store.py -132 lines, explorer.py -594, browser.py -32) so it vendored the pinned sources into /tmp/opencode/pb001_src via git show; installed playwright 1.62.0 + chromium-headless-shell 151.0.7922.34; probed both target sites HTTP 200.

The persist step pushed cycle/product/32799261473/builder@b05d8f8 anyway ('git commit ... || true'), containing exactly the architect's 5 files / 920 insertions re-committed under a build message. Any future reader must not mistake this branch for a builder output snapshot; the only novel builder artifacts were ephemeral (/tmp vendored sources, pip/playwright installs) and are lost.

Wall-clock economics of the full beta chain attempt: run window 01:53:18-05:54:36Z (~4h01m) but productive agent time was ~14m (director 01:53-02:07) + ~20m (architect 04:09-04:29) + ~3.7m (builder 05:50-05:54) ~= 38m; >=3h23m idle gaps between phases. run_attempt=3 with run_started_at matching the builder start indicates at least two partial re-runs (re-run-failed-jobs pattern); provider outage cost one 300s retry in the director phase ('Upstream request failed: Endpoint is unavailable' at 01:54:53Z). Builder also hit three 300s stall-watch warnings without abort.

Mounted lab/product base content does NOT match the architecture's pinned instrument: the working tree carried stripped-down graph/shared files while BUILD_PLAN requires vendoring from lab/graph@d41fe9b. Any PB-001 builder must vendor from Git pins, not trust the checked-out tree; the architect's INTERFACES.md/BUILD_PLAN.json encode this but it is easy to miss.
